subject: architecture
intro: Architecture leads into the built-environment professions: designing buildings, planning cities, engineering their structures, managing their construction and teaching the discipline's next generation.

roles.title: Architects, Except Landscape and Naval
roles.what: Plan and design structures such as private residences, office buildings, theaters and factories — synthesising user requirements, site conditions and regulation into buildings that are safe, buildable and worth occupying.
roles.where: The design, design synthesis and building integration criteria teach exactly this integration; technical knowledge covers the envelope, structural, environmental control and life safety systems architects specify.

roles.title: Urban and Regional Planners
roles.what: Develop comprehensive plans and programs for the use of land and physical facilities of towns, cities, counties and metropolitan areas, balancing growth, community needs and regulation from blocks to whole regions.
roles.where: The regulatory context unit — land use, current laws and the evaluative process architects use to comply — plus ecological literacy's built-versus-natural dynamic is planning's core brief.

roles.title: Civil Engineers
roles.what: Perform engineering duties in planning, designing and overseeing construction and maintenance of building structures and facilities, from roads, bridges and airports to dams, pipelines and power plants.
roles.where: Building integration's structural, environmental control and life safety systems, plus technical knowledge of construction assemblies and the health, safety and welfare criteria, are the building-scale toolkit civil engineers bring.

roles.title: Construction Managers
roles.what: Plan, direct or coordinate the construction and maintenance of structures and facilities, participating in conceptual development and overseeing organisation, scheduling, budgeting and implementation.
roles.where: The professional practice criterion — professional ethics, regulatory requirements, fundamental business processes — is the manager's ground; design synthesis teaches reconciling user requirements, regulation and site.

roles.title: Architecture Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in architecture and architectural design, such as architectural environmental design, interior architecture and design, and landscape architecture — usually combining studio teaching with research.
roles.where: The course's own arc — career paths, design, ecological literacy, history and theory, regulation and design synthesis — mirrors the studio-and-seminar curriculum architecture faculty deliver.
